title.narrative: Emergency WASH response to drought affected populations in Zeylac District

description.narrative: ltpgtCandlelight proposes an emergency WASH intervention in Zeylac District to restore safe, reliable, and equitable water access for drought-affected communities. Protracted dryness, fragile groundwater systems, and underfunded operations leave households facing long collection distances, intermittent production, and costly trucked water. The project pursues one objective to ensure that communities affected by the crisis in Zeylac district have increased access to safe, equitable, inclusive, and quality lifesaving WASH services appropriate and relevant to their immediate needs. The project target villages include Zeylac town, Fadh Xun, Sheikh Awaree and Daba Dilaac for a duration of 7 months and reaching 8,760 direct beneficiaries and 1,228 indirect beneficiaries.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project focuses on public water systems including rehabilitating one borehole (Zeylac town) and three shallow wells in Fadh Xun village (10.291242, 43.295976) also known as Habaas village in the locations tab, Sheikh Awaree village (10.444226, 43.048879) and Daba Dilaac village (10.385105, 43.256576), also known as Geelka Goojis village in the locations tab. Generally, the rehabilitation will include pipeline extensions to bring water closer to households, schools and health facilities. Other works will include installing or repairing solar pumping, restoring or constructing new storage tanks, and fixing leaks as describe further in the BoQs attached.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo ensure sustainability, the project strengthens local operation and maintenance (OM). Water user committees will be formed or refreshed and trained through a practical course covering OM planning, preventive maintenance, safety, and basic water-quality checks. Each committee will receive simple toolkits and checklists.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project further seeks to reduce waterborne disease risks through water treatment at source and households. Eight community hygiene promoters (two per village, at least one woman per pair) will be recruited, trained, and deployed to conduct door-to-door demonstrations on correct tablet dosage, safe transport and storage. Priority will be given to vulnerable and low-income households. A light post-distribution monitoring check after the first round of tablets will verify correct use and inform course corrections.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProtection, gender equality, disability inclusion, and accountability are mainstreamed. Water points proposed for rehabilitation aim to take water closer to the people thus reducing distances travelled and time taken to collect water. All the water facilities will be designed to ensure inclusivity for persons with disabilities, older persons, and caregivers. Women will hold decision-making roles in water user committees and be part of the hygiene promoters. Multiple feedback and complaints channels (including a toll-free line and scheduled community meetings) will be made available. All SEA/SH concerns will follow confidential, survivor-centered pathways separate from routine feedback.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtImplementation will be coordinated with district authorities, WASH and other Clusters at the national level to prevent duplication and align work plans while at the community level Candlelight will coordinate with other humanitarian agencies implementing projects in other sectors such as protection. Such collaboration and coordination may include but not be limited to developing and sharing similar protection messages and acting as referral points. Monitoring and reporting will use age, gender, and disability (AGD) disaggregation to track equitable access. ltbrgtlt/pgt
